conventions.convention: S is finite, while W need not be finite. Empty rank is allowed. Length minimizes word length over natural numbers including zero; the empty word represents the identity. An infinite Coxeter entry imposes no pair relator.

The splitting-field representation σ uses independently fixed primitive 2m-th roots on finite edges, c_st=ζ_st+ζ_st⁻¹, and c_st=2 on infinite edges. Positivity and faithfulness of this representation are not asserted.

The signed reflection action is a right action: (ε,r)·w=(εη(r,w),w⁻¹rw). Its reduced-word sign-change set Φ(w) consists of prefix reflections and is distinct from the geometric root set also denoted Φ.

W_Ja is a right coset, with left-descent-free minimal representative d and ℓ(ud)=ℓ(u)+ℓ(d). aW_J is a left coset, with right-descent-free d and ℓ(du)=ℓ(d)+ℓ(u). Type-A examples transport the library's zero-based labels to one-based labels; permutation products act right factor first.

The canonical real representation ρ uses B(e_s,e_s)=1 and B(e_s,e_t)=−cos(π/m), with −1 on infinite edges. No definiteness or nondegeneracy is assumed. The dual action is the left contragredient action (w·f)(v)=f(ρ(w)⁻¹v), without identifying V and V* through B.
N(w)={α∈Φ_+:ρ(w)α∈Φ_-}. For a reduced expression, suffix roots enumerate N(w), while prefix roots enumerate N(w⁻¹). Strong exchange for left multiplication uses N(w⁻¹).

C_I consists of functionals vanishing exactly on I and positive outside I; it is a relatively open face. The notation overline C_I in the chamber theorems imposes zeros on I and permits additional zeros.

U is the literal union of closed chambers. Its interior is the ordinary finite-dimensional interior for the maximum-coordinate metric, with d(0,0)=0 in empty rank. Neg(f) uses strict negativity. Local finiteness is asserted on U°; boundary points with infinite parabolic stabilizer are excluded.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite Coxeter matrix, the simple involutions induce σ:W→GL_K(E), distinct generators have products of exactly the prescribed finite or infinite orders, and the signed reflection right action is well defined. Repeated prefix reflections permit two-letter deletion. For a reduced expression, its prefix reflections are distinct and their set is expression-independent with cardinality ℓ(w). Alternating words of length q≤m for finite m, or any q≥1 for infinite m, are reduced in the ambient W.

For a finite Coxeter matrix, sgn(w)=(−1)^ℓ(w), and multiplication by a simple generator changes length by ±1. If w=s₁⋯s_k is reduced and ℓ(sw)=k−1, then sw is obtained by deleting one letter; the right-handed form also holds. Every nonreduced word admits a value-preserving two-letter deletion. The signed reflection right action is faithful.

For a finite Coxeter matrix, any two reduced expressions of the same element are braid-equivalent. A word is reduced if and only if no sequence of braid moves followed by cancellation of a consecutive equal pair can shorten it. For distinct s,t, S∩⟨s,t⟩={s,t}, and every element of that dihedral subgroup has an ambient reduced expression in s,t.

For a finite Coxeter matrix and J⊆S, reduced support S(w) is well defined and W_J={w:S(w)⊆J}. The restricted presentation maps isomorphically onto W_J, its intrinsic length equals ambient length, and W_J∩S=J. Every right coset W_Ja has a unique minimum d, characterized by ℓ(sd)>ℓ(d) for s∈J, with ℓ(ud)=ℓ(u)+ℓ(d) for u∈W_J; inversion gives the mirrored left-coset statement. In type A_{n−1}, n≥2, the adjacent-transposition map is an isomorphism W→S_n and ℓ(w)=inv(φ(w)).

For the canonical real representation of a finite-rank Coxeter system, the rank-two half-space alternative and the simultaneous assertions (P_n),(Q_n) hold for every n≥0. For every w and s, wC° lies entirely in one of the two open simple half-spaces, and wC°⊆sB_s if and only if ℓ(sw)<ℓ(w). The canonical minimal-parabolic factorization w=ud satisfies wC°⊆u(B_s∩B_t) and ℓ(w)=ℓ_{s,t}(u)+ℓ(d).

Every canonical root lies in V_+∖{0} or −V_+∖{0}, and not both; Φ=Φ_+⊔Φ_- with Φ_-=−Φ_+. For every s, r_s permutes Φ_+∖{e_s} and sends e_s to −e_s. For v∈V, v∈V_+∖{0} if and only if f(v)>0 for every f∈C°.

For every w∈W and s∈S, ℓ(ws)>ℓ(w) if and only if ρ(w)e_s∈Φ_+, and ℓ(ws)<ℓ(w) if and only if ρ(w)e_s∈Φ_-. Distinct open chambers are disjoint. Both ρ and its dual action are injective; for every w≠1 there is s with ρ(w)e_s∈Φ_-.

The canonical root-reflection map is well defined, with ρ(t_α)=r_α and t_α=t_β exactly when α=±β; Φ_+→T is a bijection. For every w, |N(w)|=ℓ(w), with distinct positive suffix roots enumerating N(w) and prefix roots enumerating N(w⁻¹). If t∈T and ℓ(tw)<ℓ(w), then any reduced expression w=s₁⋯s_n has a unique deletion index i with tw=s₁⋯ŝ_i⋯s_n and t the corresponding prefix reflection; its positive root is the corresponding prefix root in N(w⁻¹).

If f,g∈C and w·f=g, then f=g and w∈W_{S(f)}. Thus Stab_W(f)=W_{S(f)} for f∈C, with the conjugated formula for points of U. Moreover wC∩C={f∈C:w∈W_{S(f)}}=⋃_{T⊆S,w∈W_T}overline C_T. Every W-orbit in U meets C in exactly one point, and wH_{e_s}=H_{ρ(w)e_s}.

For every f∈V*, f∈U if and only if Neg(f) is finite, and Neg(f)=∅ if and only if f∈C. When Neg(f) is finite and f(e_s)<0, Neg(s·f)=r_s(Neg(f)∖{e_s}), decreasing its cardinality by one; reduction reaches C after exactly |Neg(f)| steps. U is closed under nonnegative scaling and convex combinations. If w·f∈C, then Neg(f)⊆N(w) and |Neg(f)|≤ℓ(w).

For f∈C, f∈U° if and only if W_{S(f)} is finite; U° is the union of W-translates of the spherical faces. For f=w·f₀∈U° and I=S(f₀), some ball about f is covered by wuC, u∈W_I, and meets only those chambers and their walls. Compact subsets of U° meet finitely many chambers and walls. If W_{S(f)} is infinite, f−tδ_I lies outside U for every t>0 and approaches f, while every neighborhood meets all uC, u∈W_I. Finally 0∈U° if and only if W is finite.

seams_checked.note: The page lists this prerequisite but its current items import no mathematical proposition from the tensor page. No tensor, base-change or Choice assertion is strengthened by this edge.

Checked all six external supplier interfaces and the owned uses. The real form, contragredient action, unit norms, nonempty faces and rank-two tiling clauses are preserved, including removal of nonzero infinite-dihedral boundary points from the chamber union.

The cited universal property, ±1 length laws, exchange, ambient finite-dihedral reducedness and Matsumoto clauses match their suppliers. The length-operator and reduced-product proofs use these within finite rank without assuming finite W.

The real construction uses the finite Coxeter presentation and its universal property to descend the independently computed real reflections. It does not import positivity or faithfulness of the arbitrary splitting-field representation.

Support, restricted presentations, deletion, minimal representatives and additivity are quoted with the correct left/right coset conventions, including applications inside an intrinsic standard parabolic system.

Root signs, the simple root-length criterion, the root-reflection dictionary and unique strong-exchange index are stated faithfully. The root-subsystem induction and double-coset intersection proof use those clauses with their stated hypotheses.
The right-exchange supplier quotes the full left strong-exchange clause, including the prefix root in N(w⁻¹), and derives its right-handed version by inversion and reversal.
The finiteness criterion's F7 retains f,g∈C in the collision theorem. Identity isolation applies it to f∈C° and w·f∈C°, so S(f)=∅. No local-finiteness statement is extended to boundary points.

The presentation universal property, Matsumoto braid connectivity and simple-generator parity are used faithfully. Positive lifts are defined by reduced-word independence; length-additive multiplication is established separately.

Canonical faithfulness is quoted without a definiteness assumption. The interface explicitly distinguishes faithfulness from reflection faithfulness and derives the radical-hyperplane obstruction rather than claiming the latter from the former.

The heap criterion's F3 preserves both Matsumoto clauses: braid connectivity of reduced expressions and shortening by braid moves followed by equal-pair cancellation. Infinite labels impose no finite forbidden braid block.
